text:
jess: Heads-up — canaryed Velvet-20B int8 on a small fleet yesterday. Getting intermittent OOMs on cold-start for long-context prompts (~1.1k-1.5k tokens). Not consistent but spikes at p95. Anyone seen similar with int8 + aggressive prefetch?

kai: saw something related on a Falcon canary last month. Do you have logs?

jess: pasted the tail from the worker logs: 
```
2026-02-10T03:12:45Z worker-23 ERROR oom while allocating 512MB arena block
2026-02-10T03:12:45Z worker-23 WARN kv_prefetch: requested=4 loaded=3
2026-02-10T03:12:45Z worker-23 INFO cache_compact triggered, reclaimed=32MB
2026-02-10T03:12:45Z worker-23 ERROR memory fragmentation ratio=0.78
```
Noting prefetch requested 4 segments, loaded 3. Fragmentation ratio pretty high.

nisha: how are you launching the canary? batch settings, max_new_tokens, and slow-start?

jess: canary config: `batch_max_tokens=4096`, `max_new_tokens=512` (default), `initial_kv_prefetch=4`, `kv_trim_interval=60s`, `quant=int8`  — single-request concurrency 2.

kai: initial_kv_prefetch=4 is aggressive for int8 on this model; combined with large max_new_tokens it'll blow up the arena allocator. We saw similar where arena couldn't satisfy contiguous blocks (int8 page layout + allocator slack).

nisha: is this fragmentation caused by variable allocation sizes when kv cache grows per token? If so prefetch + large max_new_tokens amplifies it.

jess: that matches correlation — failures concentrated on long prompts + multi-chunk prefetch. Short prompts fine.

ops-bot: deploy 1948887000 velvet-20b-int8-canary started (canary-id=velvet-int8-2026-02-10t03).

kai: quick experiments to try: 1) reduce `initial_kv_prefetch` to `1` 2) enable `kv_shrink_threshold=0.6` (aggressive trimming) 3) lower default `max_new_tokens` per-route to `256` for hosted routes until we validate. Also try `arena_compact_on_free=true` to reduce fragmentation.

jess: ran a quick patch: set `initial_kv_prefetch=1` + `arena_compact_on_free=true` on one node. After that the same workload had no OOMs for ~2k requests. p95 latency +12ms but stable.

nisha: can you share p50/p95 numbers before/after? we need SLA impact for product.

jess: before patch (canary baseline): p50=82ms, p95=410ms (with several hard OOM fallback retries). After patch: p50=94ms, p95=425ms but no retries and far fewer 5xx. CPU usage slightly higher.

kai: tradeoff looks reasonable — +12ms p50, p95 similar but reliability improved. If we lower `max_new_tokens` to 256 we can probably drop p95 more. Suggest per-route override: default 256, premium routes keep 512.

nisha: agree. Also let's add a KV churn metric (kv_prefetch_requested vs loaded) and fragmentation ratio alert when >0.6 for 5m. We can auto-roll back canary to fp16 variant on 5xx spike.

jess: opened PR with the config change and added a metric panel. PR: `github.com/redwood/serving-config/pull/872` (will canary after merge).

release-bot: PR merged by jess at 2026-02-10T04:10:00Z. Canary rollout starting 03:45 UTC.

kai: one more note — we observed cold-start OOMs were tied to checkpoint layout: the quantized partitioning placed a hot KV table segment at a high-address region causing larger contiguous allocations. For future onboarding, add a check in model-adapter that warns when partition_contig_ratio > 0.7 for int8 quantized artifacts.

jess: good call. I'll add a preflight check to the model artifact validator. Also adding canary test with synthetic long-context prompts (1.5k tokens) to exercise worst-case.

nisha: action items: 1) merge config change (jess) 2) add fragmentation alert (nisha) 3) add model-adapter preflight check (kai/jess) 4) update docs on per-route `max_new_tokens` defaults (product/docs).

jess: will file tickets and ping product for the docs update. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kai: nice find. We'll loop back after 24h of canary traffic.

ops-bot: canary health: 24h running, error-rate reduced from 0.8% to 0.05% on velvet-int8-canary.

jess: closing thread after 48h stable. Follow-ups in #eng-ml with PR and tickets.
